body:
WHAT
Two things must be true of the macOS build, proved on the artifact itself. BUILD: `npm run dist:mac` (app/) bundles the engine with the darwin ripgrep for the running arch and runs electron-builder for an arm64 dmg named MAGENTRA-<version>-mac-arm64.dmg, leaving app/dist/mac-arm64/MAGENTRA.app with Contents/MacOS/MAGENTRA, Contents/Resources/bin/magentra (the terminal launcher afterPack writes, mode 0755), and Contents/Resources/engine/{engine.cjs, doc-extract.mjs, tui.mjs, rg}. The app is deliberately unsigned (`identity: null`), so the documented first-open path for a user is right-click → Open; that is a Gatekeeper fact, not an admin requirement. READINESS: the built app opens for a standard, NON-ADMIN macOS user: nothing in Contents/ is owned by root or setuid, every binary has its exec bit, Info.plist carries CFBundleExecutable MAGENTRA, CFBundleIdentifier com.magentra.app and CFBundleShortVersionString equal to package.json's version, and `Contents/MacOS/MAGENTRA --smoke --user-data-dir=<tmp>` boots Electron, loads the renderer and exits 0 within 60 s (main.js exits 1 if the renderer process dies). The bundled Grep binary runs (`Contents/Resources/engine/rg --version` exits 0) and the engine bundle boots as Node (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 Contents/MacOS/MAGENTRA Contents/Resources/engine/engine.cjs --bogus` prints the host's fatal error frame and exits 1). CROSS-OS: electron-builder cannot produce a dmg anywhere but macOS and nothing but macOS can launch the app, so these tests run only where process.platform === 'darwin'. Elsewhere they fail loudly with 'macOS artifact tests need a Mac; the release workflow's mac leg is the proof there', and the workflow assertion (item 6) demands that leg smoke-launches the packaged app.

WHY
Until now no test touched the mac artifact at all: a missing exec bit (this repo is checked out on Windows, where git records none), a launcher that afterPack forgot, or a dmg whose app dies at boot would all ship green. Non-admin is the case that matters: a standard macOS account must be able to open the app without an administrator, and an unsigned app must at least be openable the documented way.

WHERE
app/package.json — scripts.dist:mac, build.mac.target [{ target:'dmg', arch:['arm64'] }], build.mac.artifactName "MAGENTRA-${version}-mac-${arch}.${ext}", build.mac.identity null, build.mac.extraResources filter [engine.cjs, doc-extract.mjs, tui.mjs, rg], build.appId com.magentra.app, build.productName MAGENTRA. app/scripts/dist.js — spawnSync('electron-builder', ['--publish','never', ...argv, -c.electronVersion, -c.extraMetadata.magentraCommit]). app/scripts/bundle-engine.js — RIPGREP { target:'mac', src: node_modules/@vscode/ripgrep-darwin-<process.arch>/bin/rg }, parseTargets(), the throw for a missing target rg. app/scripts/afterPack.js — the darwin branch writing Contents/Resources/bin/magentra from MAC_LAUNCHER with mode 0o755. app/main.js — `const SMOKE = process.argv.includes("--smoke")` (line 42), the single-instance lock skipped under SMOKE (line 48), did-finish-load → `app.exit(rendererCrashed ? 1 : 0)` after 5 s, render-process-gone → `if (SMOKE) app.exit(1)`. engine/host/src/main.ts — parseArgs() rejecting an unknown flag with a fatal error frame. .github/workflows/release.yml — the mac matrix leg (os macos-latest, `npm run dist:mac`, upload app/dist/*.dmg). tests/lib/procTest.ts — the kind these run under; tests/lib/exclusive.ts — withExclusiveLock.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. BUILD (proc, darwin only, exclusive lock 'dist', timeout 15 min): run `npm run dist:mac` in app/ with a clean app/dist; assert exit 0, that app/dist contains MAGENTRA-<package.json version>-mac-arm64.dmg, and that app/dist/mac-arm64/MAGENTRA.app/Contents holds MacOS/MAGENTRA, Resources/bin/magentra and Resources/engine/{engine.cjs, doc-extract.mjs, tui.mjs, rg}. Every later item reuses this output and fails (never skips) with 'run item 1 first' when the .app is absent.
2. NON-ADMIN READY (fs on the artifact): stat every file under Contents/ and assert none is owned by uid 0 and none has the setuid or setgid bit; assert Contents/MacOS/MAGENTRA, Contents/Resources/bin/magentra and Contents/Resources/engine/rg each have mode & 0o111 !== 0; parse Contents/Info.plist and assert CFBundleExecutable 'MAGENTRA', CFBundleIdentifier 'com.magentra.app', CFBundleShortVersionString equal to package.json's version; `codesign -dv` on the .app reports either no signature or an ad-hoc one — never a signature requiring a provisioning profile.
3. LAUNCHES (proc): spawn Contents/MacOS/MAGENTRA with ['--smoke', '--user-data-dir=<fresh temp dir>'] and a clean env; assert exit 0 within 60 s and that the app's log under <temp>/ has a 'landing-shown' event and no 'render-process-gone' event. Also `hdiutil attach -nobrowse -readonly <dmg>` and assert the mounted volume contains MAGENTRA.app and an Applications symlink, then detach — the double-click install path a non-admin user takes.
4. TOOLS READY (proc): run Contents/Resources/engine/rg --version and assert exit 0 and stdout starting 'ripgrep'; run Contents/MacOS/MAGENTRA with env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and args [Contents/Resources/engine/engine.cjs, '--bogus'] and assert exit 1 with a single stdout line parsing as `{type:'error', fatal:true}`; run `sh Contents/Resources/bin/magentra --gui --help` style invocation only to the extent that the script resolves its sibling paths (assert it references Contents/MacOS/MAGENTRA and resources/engine/tui.mjs relative to itself, no absolute build-machine path).
5. NAMES AGREE (pure): app/main/updates.js assetName on darwin arm64 equals the dmg name produced in item 1 for this version, and returns null for darwin x64 (no Intel artifact is built, deliberately — see the release workflow comment).
6. CI IS THE OTHER OS (pure): .github/workflows/release.yml's mac leg runs `npm run dist:mac` AND a step that launches the packaged MAGENTRA.app/Contents/MacOS/MAGENTRA with `--smoke` and fails the job on a non-zero exit; the windows and linux legs have the same smoke step for their artifacts. Until those steps exist this item fails — that is the point: what cannot be launched on this machine is launched on the matching runner, never assumed.
